[h2][b]"Don't make a girl a promise you can't keep"[/b][/h2]
[quote][b] Rating: 8/10 [/b][/quote]

[list][h3][b]What makes Halo a unique game imo?[/b][/h3]
[*] [b]Story:[/b] Story has surprisingly so much depth, unlike generic war campaigns.
[*] [b]Weapon:[/b] Most weapons are sci-fi and their mechanics are unique in itself. Though they have a large bullet spread.
[*] [b]Enemy:[/b] Many varieties & some intimidating. My favourite were the cute lil ones running around waving hands in the air, calling us "demons" in cute baby voice.
[*] [b]Vehicles:[/b] Warthog, Tanks, Jets, Buggy, and other aliens things with mounted guns! These are easily the best part of the game for me. Imagine you driving and your friend shooting those monsters in the campaign!
[*] [b]Coop:[/b] Yes, in campaign.
[*] [b]Difficulty:[/b] Harder than typical FPS games.
[*] [b]Input:[/b] While mouse is great, controller implementation is done extremely well. Every shock, every trigger, and every weapon feels different. <3
[/list]

[h2][b]MY individual rating:[/b][/h2]
[h3]Reach: 8/10[/h3]
[b]Legendary ending imo[/b] & felt slightly inspired from COD.

[h3]Halo 1 CE: 8.5/10[/h3]
[b]Another Legendary ending.[/b] Momentum starts to pickup and features great soundtracks! But I still hate that 1 backtracking mission with high difficulty spike.

[h3]Halo 2: 8.5/10[/h3]
[b]Insane bump in CGI & Graphics[/b], best in the series. But I witnessed many friendly AI issues in beginning. Vehicles start smoking & burning even in low damage despite having good durability.

[h3]Halo 3: 8/10[/h3]
[b]Super epic ending[/b], this was a 9 if 1st half were equally fun. I didn't like the aged graphics. New enemies they introduced were of category I hated the most. Also hate 1 rescue mission for its high difficulty & had to run past enemies to succeed. 

[h3]Halo 3 ODST: 7/10[/h3]
Rated while being generous here. It's a very diferent Halo game. Worst AAA game graphics I remember with barely visible dark world and insane level of bloom. Running around a dead dark city half the game was not that fun either.

[h3]Halo 4: 8/10[/h3]
[b]Story wise - most intense & memorable one for me.[/b] Epic opening & back to Great graphics. But gameplay flaws like we need to change weapons frequently, low ammo issues. Signature Halo weapons like Plasma pistol and Assault rifle sounded like regular pistols & AK47, bruh. Grenades were barely useful and new enemies were worse.

[h3]Halo Spartan Ops.. "campaign": 6/10[/h3]
[b]More like pesticide simulator.[/b] 50 levels where you manually select each level AND cutcene before it loads. Gave up after 10 missions and all I had to do was go there, click this button, clear area, extract! Literally EVERY SINGLE MISSION. You have unlimited respawns (no checkpoints), unlimited ammo, unbalanced enemies, rubbish radio chatter - what's even the point of this game.

[list][h3][b]Bugs?[/b][/h3]
[*] Way too many subtitle sync issues.
[*] Occasionally an enemy might get stuck in a weird spot and you can't proceed unless you play hide n seek.
[*] Sometimes getting an NPC to sit in your vehicle or another is like asking a stranger girl for late night dates.
[/list]

I didn't play multiplayer because they were not typical Deathmatch I expected, and were mostly filled with UGC content. There is a very active modding community in Steam Workshop so possibility is endless, if you are into that. I'm not.

[h3]Overall, I can recommend this game for mainstream campaign - solo/co-op 50 hours+ adventure.[/h3]

I love Halo. I have been in love with Halo since that original Xbox controller fell into my hands one Christmas morning and have been in love ever since. This collection is as close to a perfect love letter to the entire legacy of Halo that we have gotten, so far, making this the easiest game on steam that I can recommend to anyone off of sheer value alone. The multiplayer is still pretty active despite what the charts might say, thanks to crossplay with Xbox systems as well as the title being on that platform's game pass service...you hardly need to wait a minute to get put into matches depending on what you're playing (8v8 game modes might be the kind you may struggle with finding lobbies for outside of Halo 3 and Halo Reach). Having access to the original Halo Combat Evolved multiplayer with infrastructure that has been updated and now functional since this game has gotten patched up and ported to PC/steam is still such a win as the original game never supported online functionality, and it is still as insane and fun as ever. Halo 2's multiplayer is still my personal favorite but it can be the sweatiest in terms of team matchups and the competitive nature of the game as they've kept all the original online exploits in the game ranging from the button combos to super bouncing, but overall matches are still varied enough and the core gameplay is rock solid all these years later. Halo 3 is easily the most populated which is nice considering the developers have actually improved the game's net-code leading to a more fun and fair online experience however due to the lack of updates in recent years it has lead to more and more cheaters joining lobbies in Halo 3 and Halo Reach specifically, so keep that in mind. The Master Chief Collection also comes packed with forge, theater, and file share for select titles as well as full on mod support as a whole that easily extends this game's life to an unfathomable degree due to the sheer passion and creativity of the Halo modding community, there is plenty of great stuff out there. Last but certainly not least are the campaigns and this alone is reason enough to buy the game especially if you've never experienced Halo's story for whatever reason. Halo Combat Evolved Anniversary, Halo 2 Anniversary (exclusive to the Master Chief Collection), Halo 3 and Halo 3 ODST, Halo 4, and Halo Reach are all playable from start to finish offline or online with friends and as stated before, worth the price of admission alone. This game also goes on sale all the time with prices that I have personally seen as low as $10 and to be quite frank that is a steal of a deal as I am still putting time in all these years later. I cannot recommend this game enough.

I'm not sure if it's fair to call this the best Halo game that will ever be made considering it's 6 games in one. 

If you've ever had any interest in FPS games and thought to try Halo, this is probably the definitive way of doing it. 

Pros
- An insane number of classic Halo games not perfectly preserved but close enough that you'll be satisfied.
- Being able to switch between or queue up between all the multiplayers at the same time is so breaks up any monotony  you might have felt playing them back in the day.
- Between Story mode/Co-op, pvp, pve firefights, not to mention the endless amount of creativity that comes with forge it's honestly one of the best package deals for a game collection I've ever seen.
-Amazing customization for controls, your spartan and vehicles even in the oldest entries is really great.
-343/Microsoft has embraced modding to bring back things like the Halo 2 demo stage or showcase it to the community rather than pretend it doesn't exist or worse try to shut it down

Cons
- Regardless of how you feel about Halo 5, it really feels like it should be in here to complete the collection if and or when games pass goes away, having it accessible here would do wonders
- On launch and occasionally even to this day the matchmaking is functionally unplayable. You could be waiting for an hour before finding anyone to play against regardless of the number of players online.
- Not a perfect port of each game. It gets close but the slight input lag or slight differences between using the PC port versus the OG xbox versions of games. But if that's the price to pay to get extra maps/weapons/vehicles it was probably worth it
-It feels like the competitive community aspect of Halo seems to be mostly avoided in the game which
 is a bit of a shame. But after Halo 5 pushing e-sports so hard I understand.

(HALO CE (5.5/10) [1/20-1/28])

HALO 2 (7.5/10) [3/14-4/11]
A pretty massive improvement in all fronts compared to the first game. I didn't review it but, I did not like Halo CE :( The levels were repetitive and a slog to go through, enemies felt like bullet sponges, and the guns did not feel satisfying or fun to use, and it just went on for so long, leaving me only enjoying the aesthetic and only committing to finish it cause of its "classic" status in gaming history.

THIS, literally immediately from just the first two playable levels alone, I could tell I would actually enjoy. The floaty high jump giving levels more leeway, the punchier crisper gun sounds, the higher damage output and MUCH faster dying enemies, and gosh man the outskirts and metropolis setting is SO so good, what a way to start the game.

Then out of nowhere, you play as the bad guy, and it's kinda freakin awesome. Really ahead of its time, it has a main antagonist meant to go after specifically master chief and you see why he's so determined and angry and then YOU kill all the "good guys" AS him for a ton of levels and it's just really sick how they handled it. As for the rest of the story uhhh, the 3 wrinkly old guys run the show and are evil, there's a second halo ring which also is a weapon like in the first, and the arbiter redeems himself and does good things at the end, and there's a big monster that apparently is the king of the flood, that's about all I got, I wasn't too invested in the characters and the story really is a lot compared to something like Half Life 2 which depends more on visual storytelling.

But man yeah this one was good. There were some moments where you'd be stuck in a room and fight waves, or you could just run through the room of enemies and leave without fighting which discouraged actually engaging in combat, and ofc the tank and vehicle combat just don't feel good in the slightest, but besides those gripes, this is a MUCH more fun game than CE and one that I actually really enjoyed. Played the anniversary edition too and omg dem CUTSCENES, they did a great job with that remaster.

HALO 3 ODST (8/10) [4/12-5/4]
Super duper fun! So far it's my fav Halo game between 1, 2 and this, as I found the levels to be delightfully short and less grindy and annoying as they felt in past games, and the guns feel infinitely better to use than they did in 2. Ofc the atmosphere and rainy vibes of the nighttime city sections were peak as everyone says they are, and really were awesome to slowly go through even if they felt like a nothing burger walk in the local park.

But that walk felt good, the vibes were nice, they served as a good interlude before going back into the firefights, and I think the pacing and structure of the game as a whole felt perfect. Length of the game was perfect too, felt quick even though it wasn't. Story wasn't too shabby either, the timeline jumping and multiple povs of the war going down in this giant city was cool and it was fun to walk through certain areas at night right after seeing them in broad daylight covered in fire and bullets and blood which would've been only a couple of hours ago. Solid entry!

HALO REACH (8.5/10) [7/9-7/12]
Easily my favorite halo game, but we'll see how I feel when I roll credits on halo 3 cause I hear that one is amazin too. The gunplay was freakin perfect here, and the missions were perfectly paced and I rarely got lost and the context clues of when to stay in a vehicle or where to go felt very well thought-out and all the frustration and jank that I got used to with past entries has been ripped away in this one. Story was cool too, I like how full circle it feels and the ending was excellent, but rogue one DEFINITELY stole from this cause there ain't no way they're that uncannily similar by coincidence.

Let me preface this review by saying all of the games included in this collection (except for halo 4) are some of the greatest FPS games of all time. That being said I have major issues with the mismangement of this game. Therefore, I cannot reccomend it to anyone, unless you are willing to put up with a whole lot of b.s. Issues I have are as follows:

Forced Microsoft account integration (even for single player):

I have had my access to the game I purchased temporarily revoked when upo n launching the game, i was met with a notification saying that my Microsoft account had been temporarily blocked due to "Perhaps being in violation of Microsoft's code of conduct". Wherein all my access to the game including single player content was temporarily revoked until i verified my Microsoft account acrross multiple devices in order to continue playing the game I payed for. This whole process was incredibly annoying and time consuming and took over 20 minutes to get my account unblocked so I could continue playing. Note, I couldn't even aceess any campaigns or single player content during this period which is absurd.

Social Game Temproary Bans:

This game loves to hand out temporary bans that get longer and longer as they accumulate. Many players in the community are aware of this and exploit this system by shooting and meleeing their teamates and try to bait a betrayal so they can then get you kicked from a match and served a temproary ban. In my experience this form of trolling seems to be a full on passtime for some people as i experience this behavior in at least 2-3 matches a day on average, Another reason for temproary bans is disconnection from a match. Doesn't matter if your computer crashes, you lose internet access, or just quit disconnecting from even one match will result in a temprary ban. This wouldn't be much of an issue if we were talking about ranked matches, but we aren't all of this is happening in social games whiich should be meant for casual players, where there is no penalty or reward for winning or losing matches, However, this isn't the case, and you are punished by having your access temporarily revoked. In many cases i have received ,ultiple bans in a row for 1 disconnect. Example, I have disconnected from a game and have received a 5 minute ban. Then immediately upon trying to matchmake I then receive an aditional 15 minute ban for absolutely nothing. The entire system is broken, and gets exploited heavily by trolls in the community, and should seriously be removed from non ranked games altogether.

Lack of Skill Based Matchmaking:

If you are a new or returning player to the game do not expect to have a good time in matchmaking whatsoever. You will be playing against a bunch of middle-aged sweats who take the game way too seriously and will shout, throw tantrums, and cuss you out over their headsets because you can't maintain a positive score IN SOCIAL MATCHMAKING. Then they will likely abuse the temporary ban system by shooting you over and over again baiting a betrayal to get you booted from the match so you get served a temporary ban. These issues would be solved if there was any form of skill based matchmaking in the game whatsoever, maybe there is in ranked, but since everyone only plays 4-4 social games good luck having a fair match or even avoiding the toxic behaviour from those types of players that continue to treat 4-4 social like ranked. which leads to my next issue.

Goodluck Playing anything Other Than 4-4 Social:

I really like to play 8 player ffa, but that is nearly impossible because it seems the entire player base sticks to 4-4 social, it's unfortunate because this collection offers and incredible diversity of game types and playlists you can matchmake in but it seems the majority of the community stays in one playlist and it's nearly impossible to find a match in any other. I have been able to find a total of 3 matches in 8 player FFA, and that was honstly, the best experience I had in matchmaking so far, No toxic team mates, no trolls trying to get me booted by baiting me with constant friendly fire and teabagging, no middle aged basement dwellers throwing tantrums in their mics that they won't win their social slayer match. Just me playing solo against 7 other people and having a good time. Unfortunately, unless im willing to sit in matchmaking queue for 30 minutes to an hour, I cannot play this playlist, and unfortunately that's npot something I have the time or patience to do everyday.

I've never owned an XBOX console.  I had no inclination to and I sincerely doubt this will change.  

That said, I missed out on the Halo franchise.  I never even took the time to play it when given the opportunity to do so with others, however infrequent, when someone would have their XBOX over to play it on a couch situation but I did watch a few games every so often.

So when it finally came time for them to release the game on Steam, it was really a no-brainer out of interest alone.  I wanted to see what it had.  I'm not the best at FPS but I was comfortable enough with wanting to jump in head first.  It was about as I expected for the experience, that said: If it isn't the single-player content it is almost certainly the multiplayer that drives the fact home that I am 20 years behind.  

In short: I.  Get.  My.  Ass.  Kiiiicked.

That being said, that actually did not detract from the experience like many might expect it would.  Granted, I haven't really had much more than a day's worth of time on this but I've been pretty happy for what time I've invested on it, especially with others.  It's actually quite fun in short bursts and, for what little I know, it's very fun in a casual setting.  It's enough that I came back to play it over several more sessions to get better at...and for being relatively unknown franchise in my life, that's saying something.

It almost makes me regret not having an XBOX.  Almost.  Thankfully, with this, I don't need one.
